family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of string cells and a list of column widths of the same length, left-justify each cell with spaces to its column width and join the columns with ' | '. If a cell is already at least as long as its width, leave it unpadded (do not truncate).
reference:
def render_row_left(cells, widths):
    return " | ".join(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(cells, widths))

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of string cells and a list of column widths of the same length, right-justify each cell with spaces to its column width and join the columns with ' | '. If a cell is already at least as long as its width, leave it unpadded (do not truncate).
reference:
def render_row_right(cells, widths):
    return " | ".join(c.rjust(w) for c, w in zip(cells, widths))

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of string cells and a list of column widths of the same length, center each cell within its column width using spaces on both sides and join the columns with ' | '. When the padding cannot be split evenly, the extra space goes on the right side of the cell.
reference:
def render_row_center(cells, widths):
    return " | ".join(c.center(w) for c, w in zip(cells, widths))

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given cells, matching column widths, and a list of one-letter alignment codes ('l' for left, 'r' for right, 'c' for center), pad each cell to its width using the requested alignment, then join the columns with a single space. Alignment codes are given per column and lists are always the same length.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of cells and matching column widths, left-justify each cell to its width and format the row as a grid line: a leading '| ', the padded cells joined by ' | ', and a trailing ' |'.
hidden_tests: assert render_grid_row(['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'], [2, 2, 2, 2]) == '| a  | b  | c  | d  |'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given cells, matching widths, and a separator string, left-justify each cell to its width with spaces and join the padded cells together using the given separator string.
reference:
def render_row_with_sep(cells, widths, sep):
    return sep.join(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(cells, widths))

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given cells and matching widths, force each cell to exactly its column width: if the cell is longer than the width, cut it down to the first width characters; if it is shorter, left-justify it with trailing spaces. Join the resulting fixed-width columns with a single space.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of (key, value) pairs and a fixed key column width, render one line per pair: the key left-justified with spaces to key_width immediately followed by the string form of the value. Join the lines with newline characters. An empty list of pairs produces an empty string.
hidden_tests: assert render_two_col_table([('very long key', 'v')], 20) == 'very long key       v'
assert render_two_col_table([('s', 'text with space')], 3) == 's  text with space'
reference:
def render_two_col_table(pairs, key_width):
    return "\n".join(k.ljust(key_width) + str(v) for k, v in pairs)

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Split text on whitespace into words, then greedily pack the words into lines separated by single spaces so that no line exceeds width characters. A single word longer than width is placed alone on its own line without being split. Return the list of lines; an empty or all-whitespace text returns an empty list.
visible_tests: assert wrap_greedy('the quick brown fox', 10) == ['the quick', 'brown fox']
assert wrap_greedy('a b c d', 3) == ['a b', 'c d']
hidden_tests: assert wrap_greedy('one two three four five six', 11) == ['one two', 'three four', 'five six']
assert wrap_greedy('a b c d e f g h', 1) == ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g', 'h']
assert wrap_greedy('aaaa bbbb cccc dddd', 9) == ['aaaa bbbb', 'cccc dddd']
assert wrap_greedy('wrap this text please now', 12) == ['wrap this', 'text please', 'now']
assert wrap_greedy('this is a longer test sentence for wrapping', 15) == ['this is a', 'longer test', 'sentence for', 'wrapping']

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Split text on whitespace into words and greedily pack them into lines of at most width characters, separated by single spaces, like a simple word wrap. Unlike a plain wrap, if a single word is longer than width, cut it into consecutive width-character chunks (each chunk its own line) until the remainder fits, then continue packing normally. Empty text returns an empty list.
hidden_tests: assert wrap_break_long_words('short words here', 100) == ['short words here']
assert wrap_break_long_words('hi go to extremelylongdestination now', 8) == ['hi go to', 'extremel', 'ylongdes', 'tination', 'now']
assert wrap_break_long_words('multi word test case here', 6) == ['multi', 'word', 'test', 'case', 'here']

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Greedily word-wrap text to width characters per line as usual. If the result has more than max_lines lines, keep only the first max_lines lines and append '...' to the end of the last kept line, truncating that line first if needed so it still fits within width characters (including the ellipsis).
visible_tests: assert wrap_fixed_lines('one two three four five', 6, 2) == ['one', 'two...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('a b c d', 3, 2) == ['a b', 'c d']
hidden_tests: assert wrap_fixed_lines('one two three four five six seven', 5, 1) == ['on...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('just one line', 30, 5) == ['just one line']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('aaaa bbbb cccc dddd eeee', 4, 1) == ['a...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('hello world foo bar baz qux', 6, 3) == ['hello', 'world', 'foo...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('wrap this into exactly two lines here', 8, 2) == ['wrap', 'this...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('many many many words to wrap today', 5, 2) == ['many', 'ma...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('x y z w v u t s r', 1, 3) == ['x', 'y', '...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('keep all lines here please', 30, 10) == ['keep all lines here please']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('one two three four five six', 4, 3) == ['one', 'two', 't...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('test the ellipsis truncation logic now', 4, 1) == ['t...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('abc def ghi jkl mno', 3, 2) == ['abc', '...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('final case for coverage of wrapping', 6, 4) == ['final', 'case', 'for', 'cov...']
assert wrap_fixed_lines('aa bb cc dd ee ff gg', 2, 2) == ['aa', '...']

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Greedily word-wrap text so the first line may use the full width, while every following line is limited to width minus indent characters of words and then prefixed with that many spaces when returned (so its total printed length still fits in width). Return the list of resulting lines.
visible_tests: assert wrap_with_indent('one two three four five', 8, 2) == ['one two', '  three', '  four', '  five']
assert wrap_with_indent('a b c d e f', 3, 1) == ['a b', ' c', ' d', ' e', ' f']
hidden_tests: assert wrap_with_indent('wrap with indentation applied to later lines only', 10, 4) == ['wrap with', '    indentation', '    applied', '    to', '    later', '    lines', '    only']
assert wrap_with_indent('aaaa bbbb cccc dddd', 5, 1) == ['aaaa', ' bbbb', ' cccc', ' dddd']
assert wrap_with_indent('one two three', 100, 5) == ['one two three']
assert wrap_with_indent('a b c d e f g h i j', 2, 1) == ['a', ' b', ' c', ' d', ' e', ' f', ' g', ' h', ' i', ' j']

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Split text on whitespace and greedily pack words into lines of at most width characters (with a single space between words on the same line), exactly like a simple word wrap. assert wrap_count_lines('this is a longer test sentence for wrapping today', 15) == 4

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Chop text into consecutive chunks of exactly width characters each, ignoring word boundaries entirely (pure character wrapping). The final chunk may be shorter than width if the text length isn't a multiple of it. If width is zero or negative, or text is empty, return an empty list.
hidden_tests: assert wrap_to_width_char('a b c d e', 1) == ['a', ' ', 'b', ' ', 'c', ' ', 'd', ' ', 'e']

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Greedily word-wrap text so each printed line (including its prefix) fits within width characters. The first line is prefixed with the given bullet string followed by a space; every following line is prefixed with spaces of the same length as that prefix, so continuation lines align under the wrapped text. Return the list of prefixed lines.
visible_tests: assert wrap_bullet('one two three four', 10, '-') == ['- one two', '  three', '  four']
assert wrap_bullet('short text here', 20, '*') == ['* short text here']
assert wrap_bullet('a b c d e', 5, '-') == ['- a b', '  c d', '  e']
hidden_tests: assert wrap_bullet('wrap with a bullet prefix example', 12, '*') == ['* wrap with', '  a bullet', '  prefix', '  example']
assert wrap_bullet('aaaa bbbb cccc', 6, 'o') == ['o aaaa', '  bbbb', '  cccc']
assert wrap_bullet('one two three', 100, '-') == ['- one two three']
assert wrap_bullet('many words to test bullet wrapping fully now', 9, '>') == ['> many', '  words', '  to test', '  bullet', '  wrapping', '  fully', '  now']
assert wrap_bullet('keep it short please', 8, '-') == ['- keep', '  it', '  short', '  please']
assert wrap_bullet('supercalifragilistic word test', 10, '*') == ['* supercalifragilistic', '  word', '  test']
assert wrap_bullet('first second third fourth', 8, '-') == ['- first', '  second', '  third', '  fourth']
assert wrap_bullet('m n o p q r', 3, '.') == ['. m', '  n', '  o', '  p', '  q', '  r']
assert wrap_bullet('edge case bullet test here', 9, '-') == ['- edge', '  case', '  bullet', '  test', '  here']
assert wrap_bullet('final bullet test case coverage', 8, '*') == ['* final', '  bullet', '  test', '  case', '  coverage']
assert wrap_bullet('dash bullet items rendering nicely', 10, '--') == ['-- dash', '   bullet', '   items', '   rendering', '   nicely']

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Remove up to n leading space characters from each line of text (split on newline). If a line has fewer than n leading spaces, remove only the leading spaces it actually has and leave the rest of the line untouched. Rejoin the lines with newline characters.
hidden_tests:

  b
   c', 1) == 'a
 b
  c'
assert dedent_lines('\t not spaces', 2) == '\t not spaces'
assert dedent_lines('no leading spaces at all', 5) == 'no leading spaces at all'
assert dedent_lines('     multi   spaces  inside', 3) == '  multi   spaces  inside'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Split text on newline characters and prepend n copies of the given single character ch to every line, including lines that are empty. Rejoin the lines with newline characters.
hidden_tests: assert indent_with_char('no newline text', 1, '-') == '-no newline text'
assert indent_with_char('keep spacing  here', 2, ' ') == '  keep spacing  here'
reference:
def indent_with_char(text, n, ch):
    return "\n".join(ch * n + line for line in text.split("\n"))

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of lines, find the minimum number of leading spaces among all non-blank lines (a blank line is one that is empty or contains only whitespace). Remove that many leading spaces from the start of every line, leaving blank lines unchanged. If there are no non-blank lines, return the list unchanged.
hidden_tests: assert common_dedent(['    x', '  y', '      z']) == ['  x', 'y', '    z']
assert common_dedent(['  keep spacing  here']) == ['keep spacing  here']
assert common_dedent(['    one', '        two', '    three']) == ['one', '    two', 'three']
assert common_dedent(['no leading spaces', '  some leading']) == ['no leading spaces', '  some leading']
assert common_dedent(['  a', '   b', '    c', '  d']) == ['a', ' b', '  c', 'd']
